title: Provisional measurement review
notice: These are newly derived, unvalidated educational observations. The source supplies no printed answer key for this exercise. They are unscored and require qualified ECG educator review.

fields.value: Most identified ventricular intervals cluster near 47–50 px, with one approximately 90.5 px interval between the sixth and seventh fiducials. This sample is therefore not uniformly spaced.
fields.basis: Provisional positive peak-to-peak spacing in original PDF 587
fields.reason: Selected pixel gaps: 47 px, 48 px, 48 px, 48.5 px, 47.5 px, 90.5 px, 48.5 px, 48 px, 47 px, 49 px, 49 px, 50 px. These describe a short sample, not a validated rhythm classification.

fields.basis: Assumed course speed 25 mm/s; 150 detected lines enclose 149 minor horizontal intervals across 730 pixels in the observed calibration segment.
fields.reason: 12 retained positive peak-to-peak intervals have mean spacing 51.75 px, giving 142.0 bpm. Individual-interval estimates span approximately 81.2–156.4 bpm under the same assumption; this is observed interval variation, not a confidence interval. No numerical speed label or labeled timing duration is verified on this strip. This is interval-derived, not a six-second beat count or a claim of a stable rate.

fields.value: Candidate P-wave observation: Large intercomplex crests and troughs continue through a drifting background. Several wavelets occur across longer gaps and overlap the sharp excursions. A pre-spike trough, tall stroke, small terminal notch and broad descending contour can run together. Candidate crest windows are geometric descriptions only. Neither a unique P onset nor a stable corresponding ventricular onset is identified by expected timing or rhythm.
fields.basis: Original PDF page 587; independently reconciled selected-complex observation
fields.reason: Provisional deflection description, not validated atrial identity or a diagnosis. Descriptive visible morphology only. No validated atrial identity, sinus origin, electrical conduction, absent-P claim or forced one-to-one correspondence. Which part of the pre-spike negative contour belongs to the ventricular complex? Where does the terminal notch end and the intercomplex waveform resume? Are the repeated broad contours separable atrial activity, and is any P-to-QRS association justified? This describes only the selected complexes or restricted subset. It does not establish a whole-strip event census, ventricular sequence completeness, atrial identity, or conduction relationship. Qualified ECG educator review is outstanding.

fields.value: Thirteen sharp complexes with variable positive and negative components lie on continuing pointed and rounded undulations. One longer ventricular interval interrupts a cluster of shorter intervals. The undulations have no established atrial identity, continuous atrial sequence or demonstrated relation to the sharp complexes. PR and QRS durations remain held; no conduction ratio, variable-conduction mechanism or QRS-width class is assigned.
fields.basis: New independently reviewed integrated description of the exact original raster and conditional source measurements; course comparisons are contextual, not a source-authored or educator-validated rhythm key
fields.reason: No diagnostic rhythm label, validated P-wave identity, conduction interval or clinical conclusion is assigned. Qualified ECG educator review has not occurred. This is an integrated descriptive educational interpretation, not a selected rhythm diagnosis or source-authored answer. Any named teaching comparisons in the review packet are nonpreferred criteria comparisons, not the answer for this strip. Candidate identity and interval endpoints remain unvalidated. Selected-complex PR/QRS envelopes are measurement alternatives, not physiological variability or whole-strip invariants. All released QRS envelopes cross the course width threshold and establish no narrow/wide class. Existing timing, identity and sequence holds remain. These newly derived observations remain unscored and are not eligible as validated answer keys.

limitations: Wave observations and conditional endpoint envelopes remain provisional and unscored. QT/QTc, calibrated amplitudes and clinical diagnosis are not established. Selected-complex widths do not establish sequence certainty.
pr unresolved: Continuous overlapping contours prevent a defensible P identity and correspondence.
qrs unresolved: Both the onset/background boundary and terminal ventricular boundary remain unresolved across different morphologies.
No validated atrial identity or atrioventricular relationship; visible bumps/oscillations are described without asserting P-wave presence or absence.
No secure P onset and conduction relationship, and no verified individual-strip speed.
Onset/offset boundaries in this resampled raster are not validated; sharpness does not establish a numerical QRS duration.
Ventricular onset and terminal repolarization boundary are not validated; no correction formula is applied.
Per-strip gain/calibration is not verified; no quantitative amplitude is assigned.
Not derived from morphology or rate alone; qualified educator review required.
The reported rate is conditional on course timing and provisional landmark identity, not a verified per-strip answer.
All derived fields remain provisional and excluded from validated scoring.
Only the directly observed horizontal calibration segment is used. Its line count may exclude strip borders; no full-strip duration is inferred from unlabeled marks or a prior page.

Pixel-picking and grid-sensitivity allowances are illustrative, not confidence intervals. Unknown paper speed, missed events, waveform identity and phase comparability are not bounded by those allowances.
A mean can conceal changing spacing. No sustained rate or diagnostic rhythm is inferred.

Both independently measured clear bands contain contiguous 4–6 px gaps and corresponding line centers agree within one pixel. find_peaks excludes the x-range endpoints. The line arrays are interior measured calibration spans, not a full-width duration count; page 587 has a different grid phase and a different detected count.

The broader waves between x≈402 and 492 are deliberately not inserted as additional ventricular complexes. Initial and intervening pointed oscillations are excluded; their atrial or other identity remains unassigned. All thirteen distinct narrow complexes are retained.
